137.85152,34.71780.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Trans Genic Inc.. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-2.71151,53.58982.name: Fertility Fusion
-2.71151,53.58982.state: Wrightington Hospital, Hall Lane, Appley Bridge, Wigan, Lancashire, WN6 9EP, United Kingdom
-2.71151,53.58982.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-49.28785,-25.44910.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: https://clinicaconceber.com.br/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.
